properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from a review of what dynograph-foundation offers that reflow2 does not yet use (2026-08-01, at Anthony's request). Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: propagate.rs:389 ranks impacted nodes by GLOBAL betweenness centrality — `design_network()?.betweenness()`. That answers "is this node generally important in the design?", which is not the same question as "is this node relevant to the change I just made?". IP-9's stated intent is the second one.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::personalized_pagerank (already a dependency, unused) is random-walk-with-restart — the teleport mass returns to a SEED SET instead of spreading uniformly, so scores measure relevance to those seeds. Seeding it on the change's own seed nodes gives exactly the missing question.

CHEAP: the crate is already pinned, the function is exact on graphs this size, and propagate already builds the network. Small.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is a real one: betweenness is not wrong, it is answering a different and also-useful question. The existing doc comment defends it — "a change landing on a high-betweenness node has a wider SECONDARY blast radius" — which is about onward propagation, not relevance. So this may be an ADDITION rather than a replacement, and two ranking columns may be worse for a reader than one. Whether a reader wants both, or one, or a blend, is undecided and is the actual open question.

Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; this Decision records that the SHAPE is still open.
properties.name: OPEN — should a blast radius rank by relevance TO THE CHANGE rather than by global importance?
properties.rationale: Surfaced by comparing reflow2's actual imports against dynograph-graph's exports: 8 of 17 are used. This was the strongest of the unused ones because it lands on the most-read output in the system and the mismatch between the question asked and the question answered is documented in reflow2's own doc comment.
